questions.q: Five babies weigh x₁=3.2kg, x₂=3.7kg, x₃=1.4kg, x₄=2.8kg, x₅=3.3kg. Compute Σ_{k=1}^{5} x_k.
questions.e: Add the five weights term by term: 3.2 + 3.7 + 1.4 + 2.8 + 3.3 = 14.4 kg.

questions.q: Using Σ_{k=1}^{n} k = ½n(n+1), evaluate Σ_{k=1}^{20} k.
questions.e: Substitute n=20: ½(20)(21) = 420/2 = 210. (190 comes from mistakenly using n=19.)

questions.q: Using Σ_{k=1}^{n} k³ = ¼n²(n+1)², evaluate Σ_{k=1}^{5} k³.
questions.e: Substitute n=5: ¼(5²)(6²) = ¼(25)(36) = 900/4 = 225. (100 is the n=4 answer.)

questions.q: (From the tutorial exercise) Evaluate Σ_{k=91}^{237} k.
questions.e: There are 237−91+1 = 147 terms, with average value (91+237)/2 = 164. Sum = 147 × 164 = 24,108. (23,944 comes from forgetting the +1 in the term count; 24,017 comes from subtracting Σ₁^91 instead of Σ₁^90.)

questions.q: (From the tutorial exercise) Evaluate Σ_{k=1}^{50} k².
(From the tutorial exercise) Evaluate Σ_{k=4}^{92} k³.
Apply Rule 2 (Σα = nα) to evaluate Σ_{k=1}^{9} 2 (the constant 2 summed nine times).
questions.e: By Rule 2, Σα = nα. Here n=9 and α=2, so the sum is 9×2 = 18.

questions.q: Evaluate Σ_{k=1}^{5} (3k − 2) by writing out the five terms.
If A = {1, 2}, how many elements are in its power set P(A)?
questions.e: P(A) lists every subset of A: φ, {1}, {2}, {1,2} — that is 4 subsets, matching 2ⁿ = 2² = 4.

questions.q: If a set A has 6 elements, how many elements are in its power set P(A)?
questions.e: For n=6, 2ⁿ = 2⁶ = 64. (32 is the n=5 answer.)

questions.q: Given the universal set U = {1,2,3,...,10} and A = {1,2,3,4,5}, what is Aᶜ?
questions.e: The absolute complement contains every element of U not in A. Removing 1–5 from U = {1,...,10} leaves Aᶜ = {6, 7, 8, 9, 10}.

questions.q: Given i = √−1, calculate i².
questions.e: By definition i = √−1, so squaring both sides gives i² = (√−1)² = −1.

questions.q: Given i = √−1, calculate i³.
Given i = √−1, calculate i⁴.
Given i = √−1, calculate i⁵.
questions.e: i⁵ = i⁴ · i = (1)(i) = i, since i⁴ = 1.

questions.q: For complex numbers (of the form a+bi) z = 2+3i and w = 1+4i, compute z + w.
questions.e: Add real and imaginary parts separately: (2+1) + (3+4)i = 3 + 7i.

questions.q: For complex numbers z = 2+3i and w = 1+4i, compute z × w.
questions.e: Expand: (2+3i)(1+4i) = 2 + 8i + 3i + 12i² = 2 + 11i + 12(−1) = 2 + 11i − 12 = −10 + 11i, using i² = −1. (2+11i comes from forgetting the i² term; 14+11i comes from treating i² as +1.)

questions.q: If A = {4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40} (multiples of 4 from 4 to 40), what is n(A)?
questions.e: Counting the listed multiples of 4 from 4 up to 40 gives 10 elements, so n(A) = 10.
Intersection keeps only elements common to both sets. Comparing A and B, the shared elements are 5, 7 and 11, so A ∩ B = {5, 7, 11}.
Union combines all elements from both sets, listed once each: A ∪ B = {2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8}.

questions.q: (Relative complement) If A = {1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10} and B = {1, 3, 4, 10}, what is A − B?
questions.e: A − B = A\B removes from A any elements also found in B. B contributes 1, 4, 10, which are removed from A, leaving {2, 6, 8}.

questions.q: If A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {2, 3, 4}, what is A\B?
questions.e: A\B keeps elements of A that are not in B. Removing 2 and 3 (shared with B) from A leaves {1}.

questions.q: If A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {2, 3, 4}, what is B − A?
questions.e: B − A keeps elements of B that are not in A. Removing 2 and 3 (shared with A) from B leaves {4}.

questions.q: (Modelled on ℤ\ℕ) Let A = {−3,−2,−1,0,1,2,3} and B = {1,2,3}. What is A\B?
questions.e: A\B keeps elements of A not in B. Removing 1, 2, 3 (shared with B) from A leaves {−3, −2, −1, 0} — the non-positive elements, mirroring how ℤ\ℕ gives the non-positive whole numbers.

questions.q: For the same sets A = {2,4,6,8,10,12} (6 elements) and B = {1,3,5,7,9,11,13,15,17} (9 elements), which are disjoint, what is n(A ∪ B)?
questions.e: Since A ∩ B = φ, n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) = 6 + 9 = 15.

questions.q: (Commutative property) If A = {1,2,3,4,5} and B = {2,4,6,8,10}, compute A ∩ B.
questions.e: The elements common to both A and B are 2 and 4, so A ∩ B = {2, 4}, and it equals B ∩ A by commutativity.

questions.q: For the same sets A = {1,2,3,4,5} and B = {2,4,6,8,10}, compute A ∪ B.
questions.e: Union combines all elements of A and B once each: {1,2,3,4,5,6,8,10}.

questions.q: (Associative property) Let A = {1,2,3,4}, B = {2,4,6,8}, D = {3,4,5,6}. Compute (A ∩ B) ∩ D.
questions.e: First A ∩ B = {2,4}. Then {2,4} ∩ D = {2,4} ∩ {3,4,5,6} = {4}, confirming the associative property A∩(B∩D) = {4} too.

questions.q: For the same sets A = {1,2,3,4}, B = {2,4,6,8}, D = {3,4,5,6}, compute (A ∪ B) ∪ D.
questions.e: First A ∪ B = {1,2,3,4,6,8}. Then unioning with D = {3,4,5,6} adds 5, giving {1,2,3,4,5,6,8}.

questions.q: (Distributive law) For A = {1,2,3,4}, B = {1,3,5,7}, D = {2,3,5,7}, compute A ∪ (B ∩ D).
For the same sets A = {1,2,3,4}, B = {1,3,5,7}, D = {2,3,5,7}, compute (A ∪ B) ∩ (A ∪ D) and check it matches the Distributive Law result above.
questions.e: A ∪ B = {1,2,3,4,5,7} and A ∪ D = {1,2,3,4,5,7}. Their intersection is {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7}, exactly matching A ∪ (B ∩ D), confirming the Distributive Law.
A ∪ B = {1,2,3,5,7,8,9}. Removing these from U = {1,...,10} leaves the complement {4, 6, 10}.

questions.q: For the same sets U = {1,...,10}, A = {1,3,5,7,9}, B = {2,3,5,8,9}, compute A′ ∩ B′ and verify De Morgan's Law.
questions.e: A′ = {2,4,6,8,10}, B′ = {1,4,6,7,10}. Their intersection is {4, 6, 10} — exactly matching (A∪B)′, confirming (A∪B)′ = A′∩B′.
A ∩ B = {3, 5, 9}. Removing these from U = {1,...,10} leaves the complement {1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 10}.

questions.q: For the same sets, compute A′ ∪ B′ and verify De Morgan's Law.
questions.e: A′ = {2,4,6,8,10}, B′ = {1,4,6,7,10}. Their union is {1,2,4,6,7,8,10} — exactly matching (A∩B)′, confirming (A∩B)′ = A′∪B′.

questions.q: Apply the principle of duality (swap ∪↔∩, U↔φ) to find the dual of (A ∩ B) ∪ D.
questions.e: Swap every ∩ with ∪ and every ∪ with ∩: (A ∩ B) ∪ D becomes (A ∪ B) ∩ D.

questions.q: Apply duality to find the dual of A ∩ ((B′ ∩ A) ∪ B)′ = φ.
questions.e: Swap every ∩ with ∪, every ∪ with ∩, and φ with U throughout: A ∩ ((B′∩A)∪B)′=φ becomes A ∪ ((B′∪A)∩B)′ = U.

questions.q: (Trial exercise) Find the dual of A ∪ (B ∩ A) = A.
questions.e: Swap ∪ with ∩ throughout: A ∪ (B ∩ A) = A becomes A ∩ (B ∪ A) = A.

questions.q: (Trial exercise) Find the dual of A ∩ A′ = φ.
questions.e: Swap ∩ with ∪, and swap φ with U: A ∩ A′ = φ becomes A ∪ A′ = U.

questions.q: (Trial exercise) Find the dual of A ∪ A′ = U.
questions.e: Swap ∪ with ∩, and swap U with φ: A ∪ A′ = U becomes A ∩ A′ = φ.

questions.q: (Trial exercise) Find the dual of (A ∪ B′)′ ∩ B = A′ ∩ B.
questions.e: Swap every ∪ with ∩ and every ∩ with ∪ throughout: (A∪B′)′∩B = A′∩B becomes (A∩B′)′∪B = A′∪B.

questions.q: Apply duality to find the dual of A ∪ φ = A.
questions.e: Swap ∪ with ∩, and swap φ with U: A ∪ φ = A becomes A ∩ U = A.

questions.q: (Distributive law) For A = {1,2,3,4}, B = {2,3,5}, D = {3,4,6}, compute A ∩ (B ∪ D).
In the HB1 problem (16 French, 10 English, 6 fluent in both, 20 total), how many students are fluent in only one language?
questions.e: Only-French = 16−6 = 10 and only-English = 10−6 = 4, so only one language = 10 + 4 = 14.

questions.q: (Trial exercise) Maths, English and Life Skills books were distributed to 50 students, each getting at least one book: 22 had Maths books, 22 had English books, 25 had Life Skills books, 7 had Maths and English, 6 had Maths and Life Skills, 9 had English and Life Skills. How many students had all three books?
questions.e: By inclusion-exclusion, 50 = 22+22+25 − 7−6−9 + x, so 50 = 47 + x, giving x = 3 students with all three books.

questions.q: For the same book-distribution problem, how many students had only Maths books?
If n(A) = 50, n(B) = 40, and n(A∪B) = 70, find n(A∩B).
questions.e: Rearranging inclusion-exclusion: n(A∩B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A∪B) = 50 + 40 − 70 = 20.

questions.q: Find the domain of x in the equation 1/x = 2/(x-3).
questions.e: 1/x is undefined at x=0; 2/(x-3) is undefined at x=3. Both values are excluded from the domain.

questions.q: Find the domain of x in the equation 3/(x+1) = 5/(x-4).
questions.e: x+1=0 gives x=-1 (undefined on the left); x-4=0 gives x=4 (undefined on the right). Both must be excluded from the domain.

questions.q: In the standard form of a linear equation ax + by = c, let a = 2, b = 5, x = 3 and y = -1. What is c?
questions.e: Substitute into ax+by=c: 2(3)+5(-1) = 6-5 = 1, so c = 1.

questions.q: In the standard form ax + by = c, let a = -3, b = 4, x = 2, and y = 5. What is c?
questions.e: Substitute into ax+by=c: -3(2)+4(5) = -6+20 = 14.

questions.q: Solve 5x - 9 = 0 for x.
Solve 7x - 10 = 0 for x.
Solve -3x + 12 = 0 for x.
Solve 8x + 5 = 0 for x.
Solve by substitution: x - y = 3 and x + 2y = -3. What is x?
questions.e: From x-y=3, x=y+3. Substitute into x+2y=-3: (y+3)+2y=-3 → 3y+3=-3 → 3y=-6 → y=-2. Then x=y+3=1.

questions.q: Using the same system x - y = 3 and x + 2y = -3, what is y?
questions.e: From x=y+3, substituting into x+2y=-3 gives 3y+3=-3, so 3y=-6 and y=-2.

questions.q: Solve by substitution: 2x - 3y = 7 and 3x - y = 7. What is x?
Using the same system 2x - 3y = 7 and 3x - y = 7, what is y?
Solve by substitution: 3x - 4y = 18 and 2x + y = 1. What is x?
Consider the system x + 3y = 4 and 2x + 6y = 7. What happens when you try to solve it by substitution?
questions.e: Multiplying x+3y=4 by 2 gives 2x+6y=8, but the second equation says 2x+6y=7. Since 8≠7, the system is inconsistent and has no solution.

questions.q: Solve by elimination: x + 2y = 4 and 3x - 2y = 2. What is x?
questions.e: Adding the equations eliminates y: (x+2y)+(3x-2y)=4+2 → 4x=6 → x=1.5.

questions.q: Using the same system x + 2y = 4 and 3x - 2y = 2, what is y?
questions.e: With x=1.5, substitute into x+2y=4: 1.5+2y=4 → 2y=2.5 → y=1.25.

questions.q: Solve by elimination: 2x + 3y = 7 and x + 3y = 4. What is x?
questions.e: Subtracting the second equation from the first eliminates y: (2x+3y)-(x+3y)=7-4 → x=3.

questions.q: Using the same system 2x + 3y = 7 and x + 3y = 4, what is y?
questions.e: With x=3, substitute into x+3y=4: 3+3y=4 → 3y=1 → y=1/3.

questions.q: Solve by elimination: 5x + y = 11 and 5x - y = 1. What is x?
questions.e: Adding the equations eliminates y: (5x+y)+(5x-y)=11+1 → 10x=12 → x=1.2.

questions.q: Using the same system 5x + y = 11 and 5x - y = 1, what is y?
questions.e: With x=1.2, substitute into 5x+y=11: 6+y=11 → y=5.

questions.q: Solve the equation x² - 6x + 5 = -4 by the method of factorization.
questions.e: Rearranging: x²-6x+5+4=0 → x²-6x+9=0 → (x-3)²=0, so x=3 is a repeated (double) root.

questions.q: Find the roots of the equation 2x² = 3x.
questions.e: Rearranging: 2x²-3x=0 → x(2x-3)=0. So x=0 or 2x-3=0, giving x=3/2.

questions.q: Solve 4x² + 12x + 9 = 0 by factorization.
questions.e: 4x²+12x+9 is a perfect square: (2x+3)²=0, since (2x)²=4x², 2(2x)(3)=12x, and 3²=9. So 2x+3=0, giving x=-3/2.

questions.q: Solve 4x² = 5x by factorization.
questions.e: Rearranging: 4x²-5x=0 → x(4x-5)=0. So x=0 or x=5/4.

questions.q: Solve 3x² + 7x - 20 = 0 by factorization.
questions.e: We need two numbers multiplying to 3×(-20)=-60 and adding to 7: 12 and -5. So 3x²+12x-5x-20=0 → 3x(x+4)-5(x+4)=0 → (3x-5)(x+4)=0, giving x=5/3 or x=-4.

questions.q: Solve x² - x - 12 = 0 by factorization.
questions.e: We need two numbers multiplying to -12 and adding to -1: -4 and 3. So (x-4)(x+3)=0, giving x=4 or x=-3.

questions.q: Find the zeros of the equation 2x² - 3 = 0 using the square root approach.
questions.e: 2x²-3=0 → x²=3/2. So x=±√(3/2) = ±√6/2 (rationalizing the denominator).

questions.q: Solve 3x² - 27 = 0 using the square root approach.
Solve (x + 1/2)² = 5/4 using the square root approach.
Solve 3x² - 5 = 0 using the square root approach.
questions.e: 3x²-5=0 → x²=5/3. So x=±√(5/3) = ±√15/3 (rationalizing the denominator).

questions.q: Solve 2x² + 8 = 0 using the square root approach.
questions.e: 2x²+8=0 → x²=-4. Since a square cannot be negative for real x, there is no real solution; the roots are complex, x=±2i.

questions.q: Solve (x + 1/3)² = 2/9 using the square root approach.
Following on, what is the solution set of x² + 6x - 2 = 0?
questions.e: From (x+3)²=11, take square roots: x+3=±√11, so x=-3±√11.

questions.q: Following on, what is the solution set of x² + 8x - 3 = 0?
questions.e: From (x+4)²=19, take square roots: x+4=±√19, so x=-4±√19.

questions.q: Solve 2x² - 4x - 3 = 0 by completing the square. What is (x-1)²?
questions.e: Divide by 2: x²-2x-3/2=0 → x²-2x=3/2. Add (1)²=1 to both sides: x²-2x+1=3/2+1, so (x-1)²=5/2.

questions.q: Following on, what is the solution set of 2x² - 4x - 3 = 0?
questions.e: From (x-1)²=5/2, take square roots: x-1=±√(5/2)=±√10/2, so x=1±√10/2.

questions.q: Solve 6x² + 7x + 2 = 0 using the general quadratic formula.
Solve x² - 6x + 3 = 0 using the general quadratic formula.
Solve 2x² + 5x - 3 = 0 using the general quadratic formula.
Solve x² + x - 1 = 0 using the general quadratic formula.

questions.e: Discriminant=b²-4ac=(-2)²-4(3)(5)=4-60=-56. Since it is negative, the equation has a pair of complex conjugate roots.

questions.q: Compute the discriminant of 4x² - 12x + 9 = 0 and state the nature of its roots.
o: 0; a pair of complex conjugate roots
questions.e: Discriminant=(-12)²-4(4)(9)=144-144=0. Since it equals zero, the equation has a repeated (double) real root.

questions.q: Compute the discriminant of x² + 3x - 10 = 0 and state the nature of its roots.
o: -49; a pair of complex conjugate roots
questions.e: Discriminant=3²-4(1)(-10)=9+40=49. Since it is positive, the equation has two distinct real roots.

questions.q: Solve x² - 2x - 15 = 0 using the quadratic formula and find the product of its two roots.
questions.e: Discriminant=4+60=64. x=(2±8)/2, giving x=5 or x=-3. The product of the roots is 5×(-3)=-15.

questions.q: Let P(x) = x³ + 2x² - 5x - 6. Is x = -1 a zero of P(x)?
Since P(-1) = 0 for P(x) = x³ + 2x² - 5x - 6, which linear factor does this give?
questions.e: Because P(-1)=0, the factor theorem tells us x-(-1)=x+1 is a factor of P(x).

questions.q: What is the degree of (2x³ - x)²?
questions.e: Squaring a degree-3 polynomial doubles the highest power: the leading term becomes (2x³)²=4x⁶, so the degree is 6.

questions.q: Divide 4x³ - 3x + 5 by 2x - 3 using long division. What is the quotient?
questions.e: 4x³÷2x=2x²; 2x²(2x-3)=4x³-6x², leaving 6x²-3x+5. 6x²÷2x=3x; 3x(2x-3)=6x²-9x, leaving 6x+5. 6x÷2x=3; 3(2x-3)=6x-9, leaving remainder 14. Quotient: 2x²+3x+3.

questions.q: Divide 9x³ + 6x² - 30 by 3x - 4 using long division. What is the quotient?
questions.e: 9x³÷3x=3x²; 3x²(3x-4)=9x³-12x², leaving 18x²-30 (bringing down 0x). 18x²÷3x=6x; 6x(3x-4)=18x²-24x, leaving 24x-30. 24x÷3x=8; 8(3x-4)=24x-32, leaving remainder 2. Quotient: 3x²+6x+8.

questions.q: Divide 2x⁴ + 3x³ - x - 5 by x + 2 using long division. What is the quotient?
questions.e: 2x⁴÷x=2x³; 2x³(x+2)=2x⁴+4x³, leaving -x³+0x²-x-5. -x³÷x=-x²; -x²(x+2)=-x³-2x², leaving 2x²-x-5. 2x²÷x=2x; 2x(x+2)=2x²+4x, leaving -5x-5. -5x÷x=-5; -5(x+2)=-5x-10, leaving remainder 5. Quotient: 2x³-x²+2x-5.

questions.q: Divide 2x⁴ + 3x³ - x - 5 by x + 2 using long division. What is the remainder?
questions.e: Completing the long division: 2x⁴+3x³-x-5 = (x+2)(2x³-x²+2x-5) + 5, so the remainder is 5.

questions.q: Use synthetic division to divide 4x⁵ - 30x³ - 50x - 2 by x + 3. What is the quotient?
Use synthetic division to divide x³ - 6x² + 11x - 6 by x - 2. What is the quotient?
Use synthetic division to divide 3x⁴ - 2x³ + 5x - 4 by x + 1. What is the quotient?
questions.e: Coefficients (inserting 0 for the missing x² term): 3,-2,0,5,-4, with a=-1. Bring down 3; 3(-1)=-3,-2-3=-5; -5(-1)=5,0+5=5; 5(-1)=-5,5-5=0. Quotient: 3x³-5x²+5x.

questions.q: Use synthetic division to divide 3x⁴ - 2x³ + 5x - 4 by x + 1. What is the remainder?
questions.e: Continuing the synthetic division to the constant term: 0(-1)=0, -4+0=-4, so the remainder is -4.

questions.q: Solve x³ - 4x² - 9x + 36 = 0 by grouping. What common factor emerges from the two groups?
questions.e: Grouping gives x²(x-4) - 9(x-4) = 0. Both terms share the common factor (x-4).

questions.q: Continuing, what is the full factorization of x³ - 4x² - 9x + 36 = 0?
questions.e: After factoring out (x-4): (x²-9)(x-4)=0 → (x-3)(x+3)(x-4)=0, since x²-9 is a difference of squares.

questions.q: What is the full solution set of x³ - 4x² - 9x + 36 = 0?
questions.e: From (x-3)(x+3)(x-4)=0, the roots are x=3, x=-3, and x=4.

questions.q: Solve x³ - 7x - 6 = 0. Testing x = -1: is it a root of the equation?
questions.e: Substituting x=-1: (-1)³-7(-1)-6 = -1+7-6 = 0. Since the expression equals zero, x=-1 is a root.

questions.q: Since x = -1 is a root of x³ - 7x - 6 = 0, dividing x³ - 7x - 6 by (x + 1) gives which quadratic factor?
questions.e: Synthetic division with coefficients 1,0,-7,-6 and a=-1: bring down 1; 1(-1)=-1,0-1=-1; -1(-1)=1,-7+1=-6; -6(-1)=6,-6+6=0 (remainder). Quotient: x²-x-6.

questions.q: Factorizing x² - x - 6 further gives:
questions.e: We need two numbers multiplying to -6 and adding to -1: -3 and 2. So x²-x-6 = (x-3)(x+2).

questions.q: What is the full solution set of x³ - 7x - 6 = 0?
questions.e: The full factorization is (x+1)(x-3)(x+2) = 0, giving x = -1, x = 3, and x = -2.

questions.q: Use the laws of logarithms to solve for x: 5 log₂2 = x.
questions.e: By Property 1, log_b b = 1, so log₂2 = 1. Then x = 5 × log₂2 = 5 × 1 = 5.

questions.q: Use the laws of logarithms to solve for x: log 2 + log x = log 12.
questions.e: By the product law, log2 + logx = log(2x). So log(2x) = log12, which gives 2x = 12, hence x = 6.

questions.q: Use the laws of logarithms to solve for x: log(2x + 3) + log 2 = 1.
questions.e: By the product law, log(2x+3) + log2 = log(2(2x+3)) = log(4x+6). Since the base is 10 (unwritten), 4x+6 = 10¹ = 10, so 4x = 4, giving x = 1.

questions.q: Use the laws of logarithms to solve for x: 5 log₃2 − log₃4 + log₃4 = log₃(3x − 1).
questions.e: The −log₃4 and +log₃4 cancel, leaving 5log₃2 = log₃(2⁵) = log₃32. So log₃32 = log₃(3x−1) means 3x − 1 = 32, giving 3x = 33, so x = 11.

questions.q: Use the power law of logarithms to express log₂(5²) as k × log₂5. What is the coefficient k?
questions.e: By the power law, log_a(xⁿ) = n log_a x, so log₂(5²) = 2 log₂5, giving k = 2.

questions.q: Evaluate log₂8.
questions.e: log₂8 = c means 2ᶜ = 8. Since 2³ = 8, c = 3.

questions.q: Use the laws of logarithms to solve for x: log₂(x + 1) − log₂3 = 2.
questions.e: By the quotient law, log₂((x+1)/3) = 2, so (x+1)/3 = 2² = 4, giving x + 1 = 12, so x = 11.

questions.q: Use the property a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ to evaluate 2⁻³.
questions.e: 2⁻³ is the reciprocal of 2³: 2⁻³ = 1/2³ = 1/8.

questions.q: Use the property (a/b)ⁿ = aⁿ/bⁿ to evaluate (2/7)².
Use the property (a/b)⁻ⁿ = bⁿ/aⁿ to evaluate (3/2)⁻³.
Use the property a^(m/n) = (ⁿ√a)ᵐ to evaluate 8^(2/3).

questions.q: Solve the following using factorization: 9x² − 4 = 0.

questions.q: Solve the following using factorization: 2x² − 5x + 2 = 0.

questions.q: Solve by factorization: x² + 7x + 10 = 0.

A company codes customers with an 8-character code: the first 3 characters are the letters A, B, C in any order, and the remaining 5 characters are the digits 1,2,3,4,5 in any order (each letter/digit used exactly once). How many possible codes are there?
questions.e: Arrange the 3 letters: 3! = 6 ways. Arrange the 5 digits: 5! = 120 ways. These are independent, so multiply: 3!×5! = 6×120 = 720. (40320 = 8! wrongly treats all 8 characters as one interchangeable group; 15 = 3!+5! wrongly adds instead of multiplying.)

questions.q: Of the arrangements of 3 letters chosen from RELATION (vowels E, A, I, O; consonants R, L, T, N), how many contain exactly one vowel?
questions.e: Choose 1 vowel from 4: C(4,1)=4. Choose 2 consonants from 4: C(4,2)=6. Arrange the 3 chosen letters: 3!=6. Total = 4×6×6 = 144.

questions.q: For the same committee, if a particular Pharmacist and a particular Biologist must both serve, in how many ways can the committee be formed?

questions.q: Expand (x + 2y)⁵ fully using the Binomial Theorem.
questions.e: (x+2y)⁵ = Σ(5 choose k)x⁵⁻ᵏ(2y)ᵏ for k=0..5. The coefficients (5 choose k) are 1,5,10,10,5,1, and (2y)ᵏ gives 1,2y,4y²,8y³,16y⁴,32y⁵. Multiplying term by term: x⁵ + 5·2x⁴y + 10·4x³y² + 10·8x²y³ + 5·16xy⁴ + 32y⁵ = x⁵+10x⁴y+40x³y²+80x²y³+80xy⁴+32y⁵.

questions.q: In the expansion of (x + 2y)⁵, what is the coefficient of the x²y³ term (k=3)?
questions.e: The k=3 term is (5 choose 3)x²(2y)³ = 10 × x² × 8y³ = 80x²y³. So the coefficient is 80.

questions.q: In the same expansion of (x - 2y)⁵, what is the coefficient of the x²y³ term (k=3)?
questions.e: (−2y)³ = −8y³ (negative, since the power is odd). Term = (5 choose 3)x²(−8y³) = 10×(−8) = −80x²y³. The coefficient is −80.

questions.q: Find the 4th term of the expansion of (b - 3a)⁷. Using term index k=3 (since the 1st term is k=0), what is this term?
questions.e: The 4th term corresponds to k=3: (7 choose 3)b⁴(-3a)³. (7 choose 3) = 35. (-3a)³ = -27a³. So the term is 35 × (-27) × a³b⁴ = -945a³b⁴.

questions.q: In the expansion of (2x - 1)⁶, what is the coefficient of the x² term? (Find the k where the power of x is 2, then evaluate.)
questions.e: We need 6-k=2, so k=4. Term = (6 choose 4)(2x)²(-1)⁴ = 15×4x²×1 = 60x². The coefficient is 60.

questions.q: Find the coefficient of the term in x⁴ in the expansion of (x + 1/x)¹⁰.
questions.e: The general term is (10 choose k)x^(10-2k). Setting 10-2k=4 gives k=3. (10 choose 3) = 120. So the coefficient is 120.

questions.q: Continuing the same identity ⁴√(1+x) + ⁴√(1-x) ≈ a - bx² (with a=2), find the value of b.
questions.e: Each of ⁴√(1+x) and ⁴√(1-x) contributes -(3/32)x². Adding the two x² terms: -(3/32)x² + -(3/32)x² = -(6/32)x² = -(3/16)x², so b = 3/16.

questions.q: Using (1+x)ⁿ = 1+nx+..., find the coefficient of x in the expansion of (1+x/5)¹⁰ (n=10, substituting x → x/5).

questions.e: [n(n-1)/2!] with n=-2 is [(-2)(-3)]/2 = 6/2 = 3. So the coefficient of x² is 3.

questions.e: The radical needs x-2 ≥ 0 → x ≥ 2. The denominator needs x²-4 ≠ 0 → x ≠ 2, x ≠ -2. Combining x ≥ 2 with x ≠ 2 gives x > 2.

questions.q: Evaluate lim_{x→1} (x²-1)/(x-1).
questions.e: Factor: (x-1)(x+1)/(x-1) = x+1 (x≠1). Substitute x=1: 1+1 = 2.

questions.q: Evaluate lim_{x→4} (2x+3).
questions.e: This is a polynomial, so use direct substitution: 2(4)+3 = 8+3 = 11.

questions.q: Evaluate lim_{x→1} (x²-1)/(x+1).
questions.e: The denominator x+1 is not zero at x=1, so substitute directly (no cancellation needed): (1²-1)/(1+1) = 0/2 = 0.

questions.q: Evaluate lim_{x→4} (x²-7x+10)/(x²-4).
questions.e: Factor: numerator (x-2)(x-5), denominator (x-2)(x+2). Cancel (x-2), leaving (x-5)/(x+2). Substitute x=4: (4-5)/(4+2) = -1/6.

questions.q: Evaluate lim_{x→9} (9-x)/(3-√x).
questions.e: Factor 9-x = (3-√x)(3+√x); cancel (3-√x), leaving 3+√x. Substitute x=9: 3+√9 = 3+3 = 6.

questions.q: f(x) = 1-x for x≤2, f(x) = 4 for x>2. Determine lim_{x→2} f(x).
questions.e: Left-hand limit: using x≤2, f(2)=1-2=-1. Right-hand limit: using x>2, the value is 4. Since -1 ≠ 4, the two-sided limit does not exist.

questions.q: Evaluate lim_{x→0} |x|/x.
o: Does not exist since left = -1, right = 1
questions.e: For x>0, |x|/x = x/x = 1. For x<0, |x|/x = -x/x = -1. Since the one-sided limits disagree (1 ≠ -1), the limit does not exist.

questions.q: f(x) = x+1 for x≠1, f(1) = π. Find lim_{x→1} f(x).
questions.e: The limit depends only on values near x=1, not the value at x=1 itself: for x≠1, f(x)=x+1 → 1+1 = 2 as x→1 (the fact that f(1)=π is irrelevant).

questions.q: f(x) = √(x-4) for x>4, f(x) = 8-2x for x<4. Determine lim_{x→4} f(x).
questions.e: Right-hand: lim_{x→4⁺} √(x-4) = √0 = 0. Left-hand: lim_{x→4⁻}(8-2x) = 8-8 = 0. Since both equal 0, the two-sided limit exists and equals 0.

questions.q: f(x) = (x-1)/(x²-1) for x≠1, f(1) = 2. Evaluate lim_{x→1} f(x).
questions.e: Simplify for x≠1: (x-1)/[(x-1)(x+1)] = 1/(x+1). As x→1, this gives 1/(1+1) = 1/2 (the defined value f(1)=2 does not affect the limit).

questions.q: Evaluate lim_{x→0} |x-3|.
questions.e: The absolute value function is continuous everywhere, so substitute directly: |0-3| = |-3| = 3.

questions.q: Evaluate lim_{x→∞} (5x²-1)/(2x²+1).
questions.e: Divide numerator and denominator by x² (highest power): (5-1/x²)/(2+1/x²) → (5-0)/(2+0) = 5/2.

questions.q: Evaluate lim_{x→∞} 7x/(x-4).
Evaluate lim_{x→∞} (2x³-7x+3)/(x³+2).
questions.e: Divide by x³ (highest power): (2-7/x²+3/x³)/(1+2/x³) → (2-0+0)/(1+0) = 2.

questions.q: Evaluate lim_{x→∞} -3x/(x+2).
Evaluate lim_{x→0} tan x / x.
questions.e: Write tanx/x = (sinx/x)·(1/cosx). As x→0, sinx/x → 1 and 1/cosx → 1, so the limit is 1×1 = 1.

questions.q: Evaluate lim_{x→0} sin 2x / x.
questions.e: Rewrite as 2·(sin2x/2x). As x→0, sin2x/2x → 1, so the limit is 2×1 = 2.

questions.q: Compute lim_{x→0} sec x.
questions.e: sec x = 1/cos x is continuous at x=0: sec 0 = 1/cos 0 = 1/1 = 1.

questions.q: Evaluate lim_{x→0} (cos x + sin x).
questions.e: Both cos x and sin x are continuous, so substitute x=0 directly: cos0 + sin0 = 1+0 = 1.

questions.q: Evaluate lim_{x→0} (2 tan x - x) / sin 2x.
questions.e: Divide numerator and denominator by x. Numerator/x = 2(tanx/x) - 1 → 2(1)-1 = 1. Denominator/x = sin2x/x = 2(sin2x/2x) → 2(1) = 2. So the limit is 1/2.

questions.q: Evaluate lim_{x→0} (√2 - sin x) / cos x.
questions.e: Direct substitution (cos0 ≠ 0): (√2 - sin0)/cos0 = (√2-0)/1 = √2.

questions.q: Evaluate lim_{x→0} sin 5x / x.
questions.e: Rewrite as 5·(sin5x/5x). As x→0, sin5x/5x → 1, so the limit is 5×1 = 5.

questions.q: Evaluate lim_{x→0} cot x / cot 2x.
questions.e: cotx/cot2x = (cosx/sinx)·(sin2x/cos2x) = cosx·(2sinx cosx)/(sinx cos2x) = 2cos²x/cos2x. As x→0: 2(1)²/1 = 2.

questions.q: Verify the continuity of f(x) = (x²-4)/(x-2) at x=2.
o: Discontinuous because the limit doesn't exist
questions.e: Substituting x=2 gives (4-4)/(2-2) = 0/0, undefined. Condition 1 (f(2) defined) fails, so f is discontinuous at x=2 (a removable hole), even though the limit itself is 4.

questions.q: Determine the continuity of f(x) = 3x-2 at x=-2.
questions.e: f(-2) = 3(-2)-2 = -8 (defined, polynomial). Since f is a polynomial, lim_{x→-2} f(x) = -8 too. They match, so f is continuous at x=-2.

questions.q: Determine the continuity of f(x) = 2x+6 at x=-3.
questions.e: f(-3) = 2(-3)+6 = -6+6 = 0 (defined). Since f is a polynomial, lim_{x→-3} f(x) = 0 too. They match, so f is continuous at x=-3.

questions.q: Determine the continuity of h(x) = x²-x-6 at x=3.
questions.e: h(3) = 3²-3-6 = 9-3-6 = 0 (defined, polynomial). lim_{x→3} h(x) = 0 too. They match, so h is continuous at x=3.

questions.q: Determine the continuity of h(x) = 2x³-x²-5 at x=2.

questions.q: Determine the continuity of g(x) = (x+1)/(x-3) at x=3.
questions.e: Substituting x=3 gives (3+1)/(3-3) = 4/0, undefined. Condition 1 fails, so g is discontinuous at x=3 (a vertical asymptote, not removable, since the numerator is not zero there).

questions.q: Determine the continuity of g(x) = (x-5)/(x+12) at x=-2.
questions.e: g(-2) = (-2-5)/(-2+12) = -7/10 (defined, denominator ≠ 0). As a rational function with nonzero denominator here, g is continuous at x=-2 and the limit also equals -7/10.

questions.q: Determine the continuity of f(x) = (x²-25)/(x-5) at x=5.
questions.e: Substituting x=5 gives (25-25)/(5-5) = 0/0, undefined. Condition 1 fails, so f is discontinuous at x=5 (a removable hole), even though the limit equals 10.

questions.q: Determine the continuity of f(x) = (x²-25)/(x-5) at x=0.
questions.e: f(0) = (0-25)/(0-5) = -25/-5 = 5 (defined, denominator ≠ 0). Since the denominator is nonzero at x=0, f is continuous there and the limit also equals 5.

questions.q: f(x) = x+2 for x≤1, f(x) = x²+3 for x>1. Is f continuous at x=1?

questions.q: f(x) = x-3 for x≤0, f(x) = x²+x-3 for x>0. Is f continuous at x=0?

questions.q: Evaluate ∫4x/(x²+5) dx.
questions.e: d/dx(x²+5)=2x. The numerator 4x=2(2x), so ∫4x/(x²+5)dx = 2∫2x/(x²+5)dx = 2ln|x²+5|+c.

questions.e: ∫sin x dx = −cos x + c. [−cos x]₀^π = −cos π−(−cos 0) = 1+1 = 2.

questions.e: ∫sec²x dx = tan x + c. [tan x]₀^(π/4) = tan(π/4)−tan(0) = 1−0 = 1.

questions.q: Find ∫sec x tan x dx.

questions.q: Sketch y=x²−4x−5 and find the area bounded by the curve and the x-axis.
Determine the area enclosed between the curve y=x(x−1)(x−2) and the x-axis, for 0≤x≤2.
questions.e: y=x³−3x²+2x has roots 0,1,2; the curve is positive on (0,1) and negative on (1,2). F(x)=x⁴/4−x³+x². ∫₀¹=F(1)−F(0)=1/4. ∫₁²=F(2)−F(1)=0−1/4=−1/4, so its magnitude is 1/4. Total area = 1/4+1/4 = 1/2.

questions.q: Find the points of intersection of y=x²+1 and y=7−x, then determine the area enclosed between the curves.
Determine the coordinates of intersection of y=x² and y²=8x, then find the area enclosed between the two curves.
questions.e: Substitute y=x² into y²=8x: x⁴=8x → x(x³−8)=0 → x=0 or x=2. The upper curve is y=√(8x), the lower is y=x². A=∫₀²[√(8x)−x²]dx = [(4√2/3)x^(3/2) − x³/3]₀² = 16/3 − 8/3 = 8/3.

questions.q: A curve passes through the point (1,0). If the gradient function at any point P(x,y) is 3x²−1, find the equation of the curve.
questions.e: y=∫(3x²−1)dx = x³−x+c. Substituting (1,0): 0=1−1+c → c=0. So y=x³−x.

questions.q: The gradient function of a curve at any point is (2x−3x²). If the curve passes through (1,2), find the equation of the curve.
questions.e: y=∫(2x−3x²)dx = x²−x³+c. Substituting (1,2): 1−1+c=2 → c=2. So y=x²−x³+2.

questions.q: A curve passes through the point (1,−11) and its gradient function at any point is ax²+b, where a and b are constants. A tangent to the curve at the point (2,−16) is parallel to the x-axis. Find a+b.
questions.e: The tangent at x=2 is horizontal: 4a+b=0. y=(a/3)x³+bx+c. At (1,−11): a/3+b+c=−11. At (2,−16): 8a/3+2b+c=−16. Subtracting: 7a/3+b=−5. Using b=−4a: 7a/3−4a=−5 → −5a/3=−5 → a=3, so b=−12. a+b=3+(−12)=−9.

questions.q: The demand function for a product is p=90/(q+2) and the supply function is p=q+1. Find the equilibrium quantity q₀ and the producers' surplus.

questions.e: Separate: y³dy = x²dx. Integrate: y⁴/4 = x³/3+k → y⁴ = (4/3)x³+c.

questions.q: Find the general solution of dy/dx = xy using separation of variables.
questions.e: Separate: dy/y = x dx. Integrate: ln|y| = x²/2 + k. Exponentiate: y = e^(x²/2+k) = c·e^(x²/2).

questions.q: Find the general solution of dy/dx = x/y.
questions.e: Separate: y dy = x dx. Integrate: y²/2 = x²/2 + k → y² = x²+c.

questions.q: Find the particular solution of dy/dx=3xy given x=0, y=3.
questions.e: Separating and integrating gives y=c·e^((3/2)x²). Substituting x=0,y=3: 3=c·e⁰=c, so c=3. Particular solution: y=3e^((3/2)x²).

questions.q: Find the particular solution of dy/dx = xy − 3x, given y(0)=1.
questions.e: dy/dx=x(y−3). Separate: dy/(y−3)=x dx. Integrate: ln|y−3|=x²/2+k → y−3=Ce^(x²/2) → y=3+Ce^(x²/2). At x=0,y=1: 1=3+C → C=−2. So y=3−2e^(x²/2).

If log_e a, log_e b and log_e c are consecutive terms of an arithmetic progression, which of the following is true?
I. log_e b − log_e a = log_e b − log_e c
II. b² = ac
III. b = ½(a + c)
o: None of the other four choices given.
questions.e: A GP of a, b, c corresponds to an AP of their logs, so 2 log b = log a + log c ⇒ log(b²) = log(ac) ⇒ b² = ac. Statement I misstates the AP condition and III describes an AP mean, not this GP relation, so only II holds.

questions.q: The total cost of 74 bags of maize and 47 bags of beans is GH₵6184. The cost of 39 bags of maize is the same as the cost of 33 3/7 bags of beans. How much will a trader pay for 12 bags of maize and 17 bags of beans?
o: None of the other four choices given.
questions.e: 39M = (234/7)B ⇒ M = (6/7)B. Substituting into 74M+47B=6184 gives (773/7)B=6184 ⇒ B=56, so M=48. 12 bags of maize and 17 of beans cost 12(48)+17(56) = 576+952 = GH₵1528, which matches none of the listed amounts.

questions.q: In a combined class at the College of Health Sciences there were 250 more Human Biology students than Dentistry students. The number of students offering Nursing was twice the number of students offering Dentistry. The number of students offering Human Biology was twice the number of students offering Dentistry and Nursing combined. How many students were in the class?
o: None of the other four choices given.
questions.e: Let Dentistry = D. Nursing = 2D and Human Biology = 2(D+2D) = 6D. Then D+250 = 6D ⇒ D=50, Nursing=100, Human Biology=300. Total = 50+100+300 = 450 students.

questions.q: Find the truth set of the equation 2^(2x+1) − 9(2^x) + 4 = 0.
o: None of the other four choices given.
questions.e: Let y=2^x, giving 2y²−9y+4=0 ⇒ (2y−1)(y−4)=0 ⇒ y=½ or y=4. Then 2^x=½ ⇒ x=−1, and 2^x=4 ⇒ x=2. The truth set {x=−1 or x=2} matches none of the listed sets.

questions.q: Find the ratio of the sum of the first n terms of the series log x + log x² + log x⁴ + log x⁸ + ⋯ to the first term.
o: None of the other four choices given.
questions.e: The terms are log x, 2log x, 4log x, 8log x, … — a GP with first term log x and ratio 2. The sum of n terms is log x·(2ⁿ−1), so the ratio of that sum to the first term (log x) is 2ⁿ − 1.

questions.q:
Let the symbol φ denote the null set and let the set S be defined by S = {φ, {φ}}. By the above definitions, which of these statements is/are not true?
I. φ ⊂ S II. {φ} ⊂ S III. {φ} ∈ S
o: None of the other four choices given.
questions.e: S has two elements: φ and {φ}. φ ⊂ S is true (empty set is a subset of everything). {φ} ⊂ S is true, since both its members (just φ) are in S. {φ} ∈ S is also true, since {φ} is literally one of S's two elements. All three statements ARE true, so none of I–III is the 'not true' set — the correct choice is 'none of the above'.

questions.q: If the first three terms in the expansion of (1 + αx)ⁿ in ascending powers of x are 1, 15x and 90x², find respectively the values of α and n.
o: None of the other four choices given.
questions.e: Matching coefficients: nα=15 and [n(n−1)/2]α²=90. Substituting α=15/n gives (n−1)·225 = 180n ⇒ n=5, so α=3.

questions.q: Find the middle term in the expansion of (2x − x/2)¹².

questions.e: With n=12, the middle (7th) term uses k=6: C(12,6)(2x)⁶(−x/2)⁶ = 924·(2⁶/2⁶)x¹² = 924x¹² (the sign is + since (−1)⁶=1).

questions.q: Find the ratio of the term with x⁵ to the term with x³ in the binomial expansion of (2x + 3)⁶.

questions.e: The x⁵ term (k=1) is C(6,1)(2x)⁵(3)¹ = 576x⁵; the x³ term (k=3) is C(6,3)(2x)³(3)³ = 4320x³. Their ratio is 576/4320 x² ≈ 0.13x².

questions.q: How many possible even numbers, greater than 2000, can be formed with the digits 1, 2, 4, 8, if each digit can be used only once in each number?
o: None of the other four choices given.
questions.e: The first digit must be 2, 4 or 8 (3 ways, to exceed 2000) and, independently, the last digit must be even and different from the first (2 remaining ways); the middle two digits then fill in 2! ways. Total = 3×2×2! = 3!·2! = 12.

questions.q: How many possible arrangements of letters of the word THIRTIETH can be made?

questions.e: THIRTIETH has 9 letters with repeats T×3, H×2, I×2: arrangements = 9!/(3!2!2!) = 362880/24 = 15,120.

questions.q: Find a common ratio r for the geometric progression n − 4, n + 2, 3n + 1, …
o: None of the other four choices given.
questions.e: Setting (n+2)² = (n−4)(3n+1) gives 2n²−15n−8=0, so n=8 or n=−½. n=8 gives terms 4,10,25 with r=5/2; n=−½ gives terms −4.5,1.5,−0.5 with r=−1/3. Neither ratio matches any of the listed options.

questions.q: Find the exact value of x in the equation x^(log x) = 100x.

questions.e: Taking log (base 10) of both sides: (log x)² = log100 + log x = 2 + log x. Let u=log x: u²−u−2=0 ⇒ u=2 or u=−1, so x=100 or x=1/10.

questions.q: Find the truth set of the equation 3^(log_e x) = 3x.
o: None of the other four choices given.
questions.e: Taking ln of both sides: (ln x)(ln 3) = ln 3 + ln x ⇒ ln x = ln3/(ln3−1) ≈ 11.142, so x = e^11.142 — a large number, not 11.1420 itself and not any of the other closed forms given, so none of the four choices is correct.

questions.q: Evaluate log(50^(log ½) / 2^(log(5⁻¹))).

questions.e: log(5⁻¹) = −log5, so the expression is log(½)·log50 − (−log5)·log2 = log(½)·log50 + log5·log2. Using log(½)=−log2, log50=2−log2 and log5=1−log2, this simplifies to exactly −log2 = log ½.

questions.q:
Which of the following statements is/are not true if A = φ is a subset of ℝ?
I. card(A) ≠ 0 II. card(P(A)) = 1 III. A is a singleton.
o: None of the other four choices given.
questions.e: card(φ)=0, so I (card(A)≠0) is false — not true. P(φ)={φ}, so card(P(A))=1 is true, meaning II IS true. A singleton has exactly one element, but φ has none, so III is false — not true. The 'not true' statements are I and III.

questions.q: The sum of the first n terms of a series is given by Sₙ = 4 − (½)ⁿ⁻¹. Find the least value of n such that Sₙ > 3.9999.
o: None of the other four choices given.
questions.e: We need (½)ⁿ⁻¹ 3.9999. So the least such n is 15.

questions.q: If A = {x ∈ ℝ : 4^(x²) = 2^(x+3)} and B = {x ∈ ℝ : log x² = (log x)²}, find A ∩ B.
o: None of the other four choices given.
questions.e: 4^(x²)=2^(2x²)=2^(x+3) ⇒ 2x²−x−3=0 ⇒ (2x−3)(x+1)=0 ⇒ A={−1, 3/2}. For B (x>0 required), 2log x=(log x)² ⇒ log x(log x−2)=0 ⇒ x=1 or x=100, so B={1,100}. A and B share no elements, so A∩B=φ.

questions.q:

I. {x : x is prime and 7 < x < 10} II. {x : x ∈ ℕ and 0 < x < 1} III. {x : x ∈ φ}
o: None of the other four choices given.
questions.e: I: no primes lie strictly between 7 and 10 (8, 9 aren't prime) — empty. II: no natural number lies strictly between 0 and 1 — empty. III: nothing can be an element of the empty set — trivially empty. All three are null sets.

questions.q:
Which of the statements below is/are true if A = {2,4,6,8}, B = {3,4,5,6} and D = {4,5} are subsets of the set of real numbers?
I. (B ∩ D) ∩ A = 4 II. (B ∩ D) ⊂ D III. φ ⊂ D
o: None of the other four choices given.
questions.e: B∩D = {4,5}, so (B∩D)∩A = {4,5}∩{2,4,6,8} = {4} — a set, not the bare number 4, so I is false as written. (B∩D)={4,5} is indeed a subset of D={4,5}, so II is true. The empty set is a subset of every set, so III is true.

questions.q: In a class, 156 students passed Mathematics or Physics and 75 passed both subjects. If the number of students who passed Mathematics were 9 more than those who passed Physics, and each student passed at least one of the subjects, how many students passed one subject?
o: None of the other four choices given.
questions.e: By inclusion-exclusion, |M∪P|=|M|+|P|−|M∩P| ⇒ 156=M+P−75 ⇒ M+P=231, and M=P+9 gives P=111, M=120. The number who passed exactly ONE subject is |M∪P|−|M∩P| = 156−75 = 81.

questions.q: A 16-team Ghana Premier League has GH₵80,000 to be awarded as prize money. If the last-place team is awarded GH₵2750 in prize money and the award increases by the same amount for each successive finishing place, how much will the first-place team receive?
o: None of the other four choices given.
questions.e: This is an AP of 16 terms with a=2750 and sum 80,000: 8(2·2750+15d)=80,000 ⇒ d=300. First place (16th term) = 2750 + 15(300) = GH₵7250.

questions.q: Find the value(s) of the real number k for which the matrix A = [[k, 6], [k+4, 2k]] is singular.

questions.e: Singular means det(A)=0: 2k²−6(k+4)=0 ⇒ k²−3k−12=0. The discriminant 9+48=57 is not a perfect square, so the roots are irrational and match none of the listed integer pairs.

questions.q:
If A = φ is a subset of ℝ, which of the following statements is/are not true about A?
I. card(A) ≠ 0 II. card(P(A)) = 1 III. A is not a singleton.
o: None of the other four choices given.
questions.e: card(φ)=0, so I (card(A)≠0) is false. P(φ)={φ} so card(P(A))=1 is true. A has zero elements, so it truly 'is not a singleton' — III is true. Only I is not true.

questions.q: Find the common ratio of the geometric progression (√2 − 1) + (3 − 2√2) + (5√2 − 7) + (17 − 12√2) + ⋯
o: None of the other four choices given.
questions.e: Dividing the 2nd term by the 1st: (3−2√2)/(√2−1). Rationalising by (√2+1) gives (3−2√2)(√2+1) = √2−1, the common ratio.

questions.q: If the lines L₁: x + 2y − 3 = 0 and L₂: 4x + 5y − 9 = 0 intersect at a point P, find the equation of a line that passes through P and is perpendicular to the line L₃: 3x + 2y − 5 = 0.
o: None of the other four choices given.
questions.e: Solving L₁ and L₂ gives P=(1,1). L₃ has slope −3/2, so a perpendicular line has slope 2/3: y−1=(2/3)(x−1) ⇒ 2x−3y+1=0. This matches none of the four listed equations (all have constant term ±13).

questions.e: Vieta's formulas give the sum of roots as -b/a and the product of roots as c/a.

questions.e: A repeated (or double) root occurs when a factor appears more than once in the factored polynomial.

questions.e: Synthetic division is a streamlined technique specifically for dividing by linear factors of the form (x-a).

questions.e: Extraneous roots commonly arise when squaring both sides of an equation or clearing fractions.

questions.e: The product rule allows the log of a product to be split into a sum of individual logarithms.

questions.q: The vertex of a parabola represents its:
questions.e: The vertex is the turning point of a parabola, representing either its highest or lowest value.

questions.q: Which value determines the number and nature of a quadratic's roots?
questions.e: The discriminant (b²-4ac) reveals whether roots are real and distinct, real and equal, or complex.

questions.q: A logarithm with base e is called a:
questions.e: Natural logarithms use the mathematical constant e (approximately 2.718) as their base.

questions.q: Which technique rewrites a quadratic in the form a(x-h)²+k?
questions.e: Completing the square transforms a quadratic into vertex form, revealing its turning point directly.

questions.q: A sequence in which each term differs from the previous one by a constant amount is called:
questions.e: Arithmetic sequences have a fixed common difference between consecutive terms.

questions.q: A sequence in which each term is obtained by multiplying the previous term by a constant is called:
questions.e: Geometric sequences have a fixed common ratio between consecutive terms.

questions.q: An infinite geometric series converges to a finite sum only when:
questions.e: When the absolute value of the common ratio is less than 1, the terms shrink and the series converges.

questions.q: The sum of the first n terms of a series is called a:
questions.e: A partial sum represents the total of a specific finite number of terms within a sequence.

questions.q: A formula defining each term of a sequence in terms of previous terms is called:
questions.e: Recursive formulas build each new term from one or more preceding terms, rather than directly from position.

questions.e: -4 is a negative integer, so it is not a whole number. It is an integer, which makes it rational, and all rationals are real.

questions.q: Which of these sets of numbers contains all rational numbers?

Repeating decimals and terminating decimals are Rational Numbers

Every Integer is a whole number

questions.q: Which of the following is the sum of the series 1 + 1/3 + 1/9 + 1/27 + ⋯?
questions.e: This is a geometric series with first term a=1 and ratio r=1/3. Sum = a/(1-r) = 1/(2/3) = 3/2.

questions.q: If |x + 11| ≥ 2, find all values of x which makes the inequality true.
questions.e: x+11≥2 gives x≥-9. x+11≤-2 gives x≤-13. Combined: x≤-13 or x≥-9.

questions.q: Given that 7 - 3|4x + 7| ≤ -2, find all the values of x which make this inequality true.
questions.e: 7-3|4x+7|≤-2 gives -3|4x+7|≤-9, so |4x+7|≥3 (dividing by -3 flips the inequality). This gives 4x+7≥3 (x≥-1) or 4x+7≤-3 (x≤-2.5).

questions.q: Given the absolute value inequality |ax + b| ≥ c, the inequalities needed to solve are
o: ax + b ≤ -c or ax + b ≥ c
questions.e: For |expression| ≥ c, the expression must be at or beyond +c or at or beyond -c in the negative direction: ax+b≥c or ax+b≤-c.

questions.q: An absolute value equation for the temperature, t, on Tuesday is expressed as |t - 60| = 15. The high and low temperature on Tuesday was
questions.e: t-60=15 gives t=75 (the high). t-60=-15 gives t=45 (the low).

questions.q: Write the solution set of 11(3x + 1) > 11 using interval notation.
questions.e: Dividing both sides by 11 gives 3x+1>1, so 3x>0 and x>0 — a strict inequality, so the interval is open: (0,∞).

questions.q: Which interval notation represents the set of all numbers from 2 through 7, exclusive?
questions.e: "Exclusive" means neither endpoint is included, so both ends use parentheses: (2, 7).

questions.q: Which set-builder notation describes {-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2}?
questions.e: The set runs from -3 up to and including 2, so both endpoints are included: -3 ≤ x ≤ 2.

questions.q: Which interval notation represents the set of all real numbers greater than or equal to 2 and less than 20?
questions.e: "Greater than or equal to 2" needs a closed bracket at 2; "less than 20" needs an open parenthesis at 20: [2, 20).

questions.e: x²=49 gives x=±7, i.e. {7,-7}; none of the originally printed choices state this correctly.

questions.e: Factoring gives (s+4)(s-1)=0, so s=-4 or s=1 — two different rational solutions.

questions.e: This factors as (t+4)²=0, giving a single repeated rational root t=-4.

questions.e: Rearranged: 5y²-6y=0, so y(5y-6)=0, giving y=0 or y=6/5 — two distinct rational solutions.

questions.e: A discriminant of exactly 0 gives a single repeated (double) real root, i.e. two equal roots.

questions.q: Solve for x algebraically if 3!(x-1)!/(x-3)! = 72
questions.e: 3! = 6, and (x-1)!/(x-3)! = (x-1)(x-2) for x ≥ 3. So 6(x-1)(x-2) = 72, giving (x-1)(x-2)=12, i.e. x²-3x-10=0, factoring to (x-5)(x+2)=0. Only x=5 keeps x-3 ≥ 0 for the factorials to be defined, so x=5 is the valid solution.

questions.q: In a combined class at the School of Medicine and Dentistry there were 250 more Human Biology students than Dentistry students. The number of students offering Nursing was twice the number of students offering Dentistry. The number of students offering Human Biology was twice the number of students offering Dentistry and Nursing combined. How many students were in the class?
o: None of the other four choices.
questions.e: Let D = Dentistry. Nursing = 2D. Human Biology = D + 250, and also = 2(D + 2D) = 6D. So D + 250 = 6D, giving D = 50. Then Nursing = 100 and Human Biology = 300, for a class total of 50 + 100 + 300 = 450.
